name: Commercial renovation vs tenant improvement: which is more expensive?

mainEntity.name: Which is usually more expensive, a commercial renovation or a tenant improvement?
mainEntity.text: Which is usually more expensive, a commercial renovation or a tenant improvement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither label guarantees a lower price. A tenant improvement may be relatively inexpensive if it is mostly interior finishes, partitions, and minor mechanical adjustments. A commercial renovation can be much more expensive if it includes structural repairs, exterior work, code upgrades, or major system replacements. Tenant improvements also become costly when they require plumbing, HVAC, fire protection, or accessibility changes. In Los Angeles and nearby cities, the permit path and building age can influence cost just as much as the construction scope. Owners should compare projects based on what is actually included, not just whether the work is called a renovation or a tenant improvement. The most reliable way to compare is to request a detailed scope breakdown and identify hard costs, soft costs, and contingency separately.
acceptedAnswer.description: A commercial renovation is often more expensive when it affects multiple systems, structure, or exterior elements. Tenant improvements can be less expensive if they are limited to interior finishes and layout changes, but they become costly when plumbing, HVAC, fire protection, or accessibility upgrades are included. The real cost depends on scope, not the label.
